newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia brushes off U.S. criticism over medal.
newsitem.headline: Croatia brushes off U.S. criticism over medal.

text.p: Croatia on Thursday rejected U.S. criticism of its award of a medal to a Bosnian Croat general accused of war crimes because the decision to honour him was made before he was indicted.

Washington blasted Croatia for decorating General Tihomir Blaskic, who was charged with crimes against Moslems during the Moslem-Croat war in 1992-93 when he was commander of Bosnian Croat forces in central Bosnia.

State Department deputy spokesman Glyn Davies described the move as "wholly inappropriate" in sending a signal of support to Blaskic and questioning Croatia's commitment to the Bosnian peace agreement.
A Croatian foreign ministry statement said President Franjo Tudjman awarded Blaskic the medal, for services in Croatia, a month before he was indicted by the U.N. war crimes tribunal in 1995.
The general surrendered to the tribunal in The Hague in April and the medal was received by his wife at a ceremony in a Croat-held part of Bosnia last Saturday.
Blaskic was decorated, together with thousands of Bosnian Croat soldiers, for Croatia's 1995 recapture of a rebel Serb enclave in southern Croatia.
Shortly after the tribunal pressed charges against Blaskic Tudjman promoted him to a senior post in Croatia's regular army, a move widely criticised at the time.

"It is physically impossible to give medals to over 10,000 people at once. So one has to draw up a plan. Now those medals, awarded more than a year ago, have been handed out to many soldiers, including Blaskic," a ministry official told Reuters.
The war crimes court has indicted over 70 Serbs, Croats and Moslems for alleged war crimes but has only seven in custody. Blaskic's trial is due to begin in the spring.
